In the subgroup programmed with anatomically distant poles (MPP-AS), 87% of patients were responders at 9 months. All non-responders at 3 months in this subgroup had become responders at 9 months. These data remain subgroup analyses: the superiority of MPP over conventional CRT has not been demonstrated in general. The 2021 ESC guidelines contain no recommendation in favour of routine use of MPP.
prog-ma-051.aRetenir: MPP is non-inferior to conventional CRT; the benefit appears greater with widely spaced LV poles.

prog-ma-052.question: What does the CorVue feature of Abbott ICDs and CRT-Ds monitor?
options: Day-to-day variations in thoracic impedance
Heart sounds and respiration, combined in a composite index
Minute ventilation used for rate-adaptive pacing
Pulmonary artery pressure transmitted by an implanted sensor
commentaires: Correct: CorVue tracks thoracic impedance; a persistent fall (8 to 18 days, programmable on the Gallant) triggers the alert.
Incorrect: the index combining heart sounds and respiration is HeartLogic (Boston Scientific).
Incorrect: minute ventilation is a rate-response sensor (Boston Scientific), not congestion monitoring.
Incorrect: pulmonary artery pressure is measured with a dedicated implantable sensor, separate from the ICD.
prog-ma-052.explication: CorVue is Abbott's equivalent of OptiVol: it tracks the thoracic impedance measured by the device over time. A persistent fall suggests fluid accumulation. The alert threshold is expressed as a number of consecutive days of decrease, programmable from 8 to 18 days on the Gallant. Pulmonary artery pressure is measured with a dedicated implantable sensor, separate from the ICD, and the composite heart sounds + respiration index corresponds to HeartLogic (Boston Scientific). As with OptiVol, a CorVue alert must be interpreted against the clinical picture (weight, signs of congestion, medication) to limit false positives.
prog-ma-052.aRetenir: CorVue monitors thoracic impedance; a prolonged fall suggests congestion.

prog-ma-053.question: How do the two capsules of the Aveir DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker achieve atrioventricular synchrony?
prog-ma-053.reponseAttendue: Through implant-to-implant (i2i) communication: brief, high-frequency, subthreshold electrical pulses are transmitted by conduction through the blood between the atrial capsule and the ventricular capsule. Communication is bidirectional and occurs on every beat, allowing leadless DDD operation.
prog-ma-053.explication: The Aveir DR combines a capsule in the right atrium and a capsule in the RV. They exchange information beat by beat using i2i technology, which relies on the electrical conductivity of blood, with neither radiofrequency nor an accelerometer. In the i2i study, more than 90% of beats were successfully transmitted in both directions, from implantation to 6 months. The pivotal trial showed AV synchrony of at least 70% in 97.3% of patients at 3 months. To be distinguished from Micra AV (Medtronic), which infers atrial contraction from a mechanical signal picked up by the accelerometer, with a single ventricular capsule.
prog-ma-053.aRetenir: Aveir DR: two capsules synchronised beat by beat by i2i communication, conducted through the blood.

prog-ma-054.question: In the pivotal trial of the Aveir DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker (300 patients), what were the main results at 3 months?
options: AV synchrony close to that of Micra AV, i.e. about 85% at rest
90.3% complication-free; AV synchrony ≥ 70% in 97.3% of patients
Safety endpoint not met because of frequent atrial perforations
98.3% successful implants, but AV synchrony ≥ 70% in only 60%
commentaires: Incorrect: about 85% at rest is the figure for Micra AV in AccelAV; the Aveir DR, with its atrial capsule, does better.
Correct: 90.3% complication-free at 90 days and AV synchrony ≥ 70% (sitting position) in 97.3% of patients.
Incorrect: the safety endpoint was met (90.3%, above the 78% goal), although serious complications did occur.
Incorrect: the implant rate is correct, but AV synchrony ≥ 70% was achieved in 97.3% of patients.
prog-ma-054.explication: Implantation was successful in 98.3% of patients: two functioning capsules with established i2i communication. The safety endpoint (freedom from device- or procedure-related complications at 90 days) was met in 90.3% of patients, above the 78% goal. The mean atrial threshold was 0.82 V and the mean P wave 3.58 mV. AV synchrony of at least 70% was achieved in 97.3% of patients, well beyond what mechanical sensing with Micra AV allows (about 85% at rest in AccelAV). There were, however, 35 serious events in 29 patients: complications do occur, hence the importance of long-term follow-up.
prog-ma-054.aRetenir: Aveir DR: 90.3% complication-free and 97.3% with adequate AV synchrony at 3 months.

prog-ma-055.question: Which features distinguish the Abbott Aveir VR ventricular capsule? (select all that apply)
options: Active fixation with a helix (screw-in)
Rate response via an accelerometer, like the Micra
Measurement of electrical parameters (mapping) before final fixation
Fixation with nitinol tines
commentaires: Correct: the Aveir VR screws into the myocardium, which facilitates repositioning and retrieval.
Incorrect: the Aveir VR adapts its rate based on blood temperature; the accelerometer is the Micra's sensor.
Correct: threshold, sensing and impedance are measured in contact with the site before screwing in.
Incorrect: nitinol tines are the fixation mechanism of the Micra (Medtronic).
prog-ma-055.explication: The Aveir VR is fixed by a helix screwed into the myocardium. Unlike the Micra's nitinol tines, the helix makes repositioning and retrieval easier: the capsule was designed to be retrievable. The system allows threshold, sensing and impedance to be measured in contact with the site before screwing in: this is "mapping" before fixation. Its rate response relies on a blood temperature sensor, whereas the Micra uses an accelerometer. The Aveir VR is also the ventricular component of the Aveir DR. The results of the LEADLESS II phase 2 trial demonstrated its efficacy and safety in VVIR.
prog-ma-055.aRetenir: Aveir VR: helix fixation, electrical mapping before fixation, temperature-based rate response; nitinol tines and an accelerometer are specific to the Micra.

prog-ma-056.question: What is distinctive about remote monitoring with the Abbott Confirm Rx insertable cardiac monitor?
options: Transmission via a bedside modem connected to a landline
No remote monitoring: data are reviewed in clinic only
Automatic daily transmission via a dedicated bedside transmitter
Direct transmission via the patient's smartphone (Bluetooth)
commentaires: Incorrect: landline transmission corresponds to the first generations of remote monitoring.
Incorrect: the Confirm Rx is remotely monitored; indeed, it is one of the first monitors to connect to a smartphone.
Incorrect: a dedicated bedside transmitter is the model of earlier generations and of other systems (e.g. Home Monitoring).
Correct: the Confirm Rx transmits via Bluetooth Low Energy through the myMerlin app, with no bedside unit.
prog-ma-056.explication: The Confirm Rx was one of the first insertable cardiac monitors to connect directly to the patient's smartphone via Bluetooth Low Energy, using the dedicated app. Tracings are transmitted to the follow-up centre without a bedside unit. Its algorithm was subsequently improved by a software update (SharpSense), which markedly reduced false bradycardia and pause detections. The bedside transmitter and landline correspond to older generations of remote monitoring. Pitfall: transmission depends on the phone (battery, Bluetooth, app updates), which must be explained to the patient.
prog-ma-056.aRetenir: The Confirm Rx transmits via the patient's smartphone (Bluetooth), with no bedside transmitter.

prog-ma-057.question: The Micra VR (Medtronic) is a leadless pacemaker implanted via the femoral route and fixed in the right ventricle by a helix (screw-in), whose rate response uses an accelerometer.
options: True
False
commentaires: Incorrect: the femoral route and the accelerometer are correct, but the Micra is fixed by nitinol tines; the helix is the fixation mechanism of the Aveir (Abbott).
Correct: the Micra is fixed by four nitinol tines; the screw-in helix is characteristic of the Abbott Aveir VR.
prog-ma-057.explication: This is false, because of the fixation mechanism. The Micra is a capsule implanted via the femoral vein and fixed in the RV by nitinol tines; helix fixation is that of the Abbott Aveir VR. It paces in VVI(R), and rate response does rely on its accelerometer. The pivotal study (NEJM 2016) showed an implant success rate of 99.2% and a major complication rate lower than that of a historical cohort of transvenous pacemakers. On the Micra AV, the same accelerometer is used to detect atrial contraction. Pitfall: the Micra VR does not sense the atrium and is unsuitable when AV synchrony is essential.
prog-ma-057.aRetenir: Micra: RV capsule implanted via the femoral route, fixed by nitinol tines, VVIR with accelerometer-based rate response.

prog-ma-058.question: In a patient with a Micra AV and complete AV block, AV synchrony falls markedly on exertion. What is the most likely physiological explanation?
options: A fall in the amplitude of the far-field P wave recorded by the capsule
T-wave oversensing inhibiting pacing on exertion
Loss of ventricular capture due to a rise in threshold on exertion
Fusion of the A3 and A4 mechanical signals as the sinus rate rises
commentaires: Incorrect: Micra AV does not sense the electrical P wave; it identifies atrial contraction using the accelerometer.
Incorrect: T-wave oversensing would inhibit pacing; it does not explain a selective loss of synchrony on exertion.
Incorrect: loss of capture would produce spikes not followed by a QRS, not a loss of synchrony with effective pacing.
Correct: diastole shortens, A3 (passive filling) and A4 (atrial contraction) move closer together and then fuse, and A4 is sensed less reliably.
prog-ma-058.explication: Micra AV identifies atrial contraction by a mechanical signal (A4) sensed by the accelerometer after the end of passive filling (A3). As the rate increases, diastole shortens and the A3 and A4 signals move closer together and then fuse: A4 sensing becomes less reliable. The device then paces more often without atrial synchronisation, at the programmed lower rate. In AccelAV, AV synchrony was 85.4% at rest but 74.8% during ambulatory conditions, and programming optimisation improved it. Predictors of good synchrony were studied in MARVEL 2 (A4 amplitude, among others).
prog-ma-058.aRetenir: Micra AV: at high rates, A3/A4 fusion degrades mechanical atrial sensing and hence AV synchrony.

prog-ma-059.question: After the SharpSense software update of the Confirm Rx insertable cardiac monitor, what effect was observed in real-world use?
options: More false AF detections, for lack of a P-wave discriminator
A sharp fall in false bradycardia and pause detections
Addition of backup bradycardia pacing in the event of a pause
A move from a bedside transmitter to smartphone transmission
commentaires: Incorrect: on the contrary, SharpSense added a P-wave discriminator that improves AF detection.
Correct: bradycardia detections −86.8% and pause detections −93.1%, with a sharp fall in false positives.
Incorrect: an insertable cardiac monitor never paces; it is purely diagnostic.
Incorrect: the Confirm Rx already transmitted via smartphone; SharpSense is an update of the detection algorithm.
prog-ma-059.explication: In the analysis of 197 Confirm Rx monitors followed for 90 days before and after the SharpSense update, bradycardia detections fell by 86.8% and pause detections by 93.1%. False-positive episodes fell by 91.5% for bradycardia and by 82.8% for pauses. SharpSense also improved AF detection thanks to a P-wave discriminator, evaluated in real-world use in the UK Confirm Rx study. An insertable cardiac monitor never paces. For remote monitoring teams, fewer false positives means a much lighter review workload.
prog-ma-059.aRetenir: SharpSense markedly reduced false-positive bradycardia and pause detections with the Confirm Rx.
